abstract.para: Learn how to manage files, access removable media and use assistive technologies in &gnome; Desktop.

section.title: Managing files and directories
section.para: The &nautilus; application provides a graphical interface for managing local and remote files. To launch it, press , search for files and select Files from the hit list.
The main interface elements include the following:

listitem.para: Includes back/forward navigation, a path bar with search function, view options (list or grid), sort controls and a three-dot menu for actions and settings specific to the current folder.
Provides quick access to frequently used folders and network locations. Toggle the sidebar with F9.
The three-line icon at the top of the sidebar provides options like preferences, icon size, new folders, new windows and tabs.
Displays files and folders in the selected view. Use the toolbar's view menu (top right) to switch between grid and list layouts.
Right-click items or empty space to open a menu. Options depend on where you click—on a file or folder, or on the background.

section.title: Useful key combinations
section.para: The following table lists a selection of key combinations of &nautilus;.

entry.para: Switch the path bar from a button view to an editable text box.

The editable path bar supports the URI schema and can connect to remote servers via FTP, SFTP, SSH, SMB and other protocols. For example, use ftp://tux@ftp.example.tld to connect to an FTP server ftp.example.tld with the user name tux.

listitem.para: Right-click a directory, select Compress, choose an archive format (.zip, .tar.xz or .7z), then specify a destination.
Navigate to the folder or file you want to bookmark and click the star icon to the right of its name. Bookmarked items are listed under Starred in the sidebar, where they can be renamed or reordered.

section.title: Accessing removable media
section.para: To access USB flash drives, CDs or DVDs, insert or attach the medium. An icon for the medium is automatically created on the desktop. For many media types, a Files window pops up automatically. If it doesn't, open Files and select the device in the sidebar.

warning.title: Unmount to prevent data loss
warning.para: Do not physically remove devices immediately after use. Even when no write activity is indicated, the drive may not have finished a previous operation.

step.para: From the Activities overview, open Files.
Locate the device in the sidebar and click the Eject icon.
Now you can safely remove the device.

section.title: Assistive technologies
section.para: The &gnome; Desktop provides built-in assistive technologies for users with disabilities, including low vision or impaired motor skills.

section.title: Enabling assistive technologies
section.para: To configure accessibility features, open the Settings dialog by right-clicking the desktop and choosing Settings. In the navigation pane, select Accessibility. Each assistive feature can be enabled separately. To get quick access, turn on Always Show Accessibility Menu to display a person icon in the top bar.

listitem.para: Screen Reader reads displayed text as the focus moves.
High Contrast increases color contrast of foreground and background interface elements.
On/Off Shapes uses shapes to indicate state in addition to, or instead of, using color.
Animation Effects enables visual animations throughout the user interface. Disabling it can reduce visual distraction.
Large Text increases the size of all text in the user interface.
Cursor Size improves pointer visibility.
Sound Keys play a sound when Num Lock or Caps Lock is toggled.
Always Show Scrollbars keeps scrollbars visible at all times.

section.title: Hearing assistance Hearing
section.para: Overamplification allows the system volume to exceed 100%, which can help users with hearing loss. Note that this may reduce sound quality.
Visual Alerts shows a visual indication when an alert sound occurs. You can choose to flash either the window title or the entire screen. Use Test Flash to preview the effect.

listitem.para: Screen Keyboard shows an on-screen keyboard at the bottom of the screen the next time you type.

textobject.phrase: &gnome;: on-screen keyboard turned on, showing the English alphabet and digits

listitem.para: To enter numbers and symbols, press the ?123 button first. More symbols are available if you press the =/< button. To return to the alphabetic keyboard, press the ABC button.

To temporarily hide the keyboard, press the button with the arrow down icon. The keyboard is shown again automatically in the next situation where you can use it. To change your keyboard layout or change Region & Language settings, press the button with the flag icon.
Enable by Keyboard turns accessibility features on or off using the keyboard.
Cursor Blinking controls if the cursor blinks in text fields.
Blink Speed adjusts the speed at which the cursor blinks, from Slow to Fast.
Repeat Keys repeats a key while it is held down.

Sticky Keys lets you enter key combinations one key at a time. For example, with Sticky Keys on, press
to switch windows.
With sticky keys turned off, you need to hold down both keys at the same time. With sticky keys turned on, press and then to do the same.

Slow Keys adds a delay between when a key is pressed and when it is accepted. This means that you need to hold down each key you want to type for a little while before it appears. Use slow keys if you accidentally press several keys at a time when you type, or if you find it difficult to press the right key on the keyboard first time.

Bounce Keys ignores key presses that are rapidly repeated. This feature can help, for example, if you have hand tremors which cause you to press a key multiple times when you only want to press it once.

section.title: Pointing and Clicking
section.para: In the Pointing and Clicking section of the Accessibility settings, you can enable and configure features that help people with mobility impairments related to using a mouse or other pointing devices.

listitem.para: Mouse Keys moves the mouse pointer with the numeric keypad.
Locate Pointer reveals the pointer location when you press the Left Ctrl key.
Activate Windows on Hover activates a window when you place the pointer it.
Double-Click Delay adjusts the time allowed between clicks for them to be recognized as a double-click.

Simulated Secondary Click performs a secondary click (usually equivalent to a right mouse button click) by holding the primary mouse button. This is useful if you find it difficult to move your fingers individually on one hand, or if your pointing device only has a single button.
Hover Click triggers a click by hovering the mouse pointer over an item on the screen. This is useful if you find it difficult to move the mouse and click at the same time.

If this feature is turned on, a small hover click window may open and stay above all your other windows, allowing you to choose what type of click should happen when you hover. When you hover your mouse pointer over a button and do not move it, the pointer gradually changes color. When it has fully changed color, the button is clicked.

section.title: Zoom
section.para: In the Zoom section of the Accessibility settings, you can enable features that help people with visual impairments.

listitem.para: Desktop Zoom magnifies the entire screen.
Magnifier offers detailed configuration options, including Magnifier View, Screen Area and Follow Behavior.
The Crosshairs includes options like Overlap Mouse Cursor, Thickness and Length sliders, and Color.
Color Filters offers Inverted to invert colors in the magnifier region, plus Brightness, Contrast and Color options to adjust color effects.

section.title: Installing and updating software with &gnome; Software
section.para: &productname; &productnumber; ships &gnome; Software (gnome-software) as part of the software stack. Use it to receive desktop notifications about available updates, install applications, and install and update Flatpak applications from the &gnome; graphical interface.

note.title: Reboot required for critical updates
note.para: Critical updates such as kernel, firmware or driver updates still require a reboot. &gnome; Software indicates when a restart is needed to complete an update.

section.title: How to install and update software

textobject.phrase: &gnome; Software: main window showing available applications

step.para: Open &gnome; Software from the Activities overview: Press , type software and select Software.
To install an application, find it with the search function or by browsing, open it and click Install.
To update, open the Updates tab and install the available updates. Updates that do not need a reboot are applied immediately. If a reboot is needed, restart using the Power Off menu (see ).

section.title: Managing Flatpak applications
section.para: &gnome; Software manages Flatpak applications, including installation, update notifications and updates. This also applies to Flatpak applications that cannot be detected by other management tools.

note.title: Transactional (immutable) systems
note.para: On transactional systems, the PackageKit plug-in of &gnome; Software detects the environment and disables itself. This prevents failed update operations on the read-only root file system. &gnome; Software can still manage Flatpak applications. Manage system packages with the transactional-update tool instead.
